subtopics.title: The Cold Wind You Felt This Morning

questions.question: What is the general geographical location where mid-latitude cyclones develop?
options: Between 30° and 60° north and south of the equator
Right on the equator (0°)
Directly over the North and South Poles (90°)
Between 0° and 30° north and south of the equator

questions.question: Which two air masses meet to form a mid-latitude cyclone that affects South Africa?
options: Warm tropical air and cold polar air from Antarctica
Warm air from the equator and warm air from the desert
Cold air from the ocean and cold air from the land
Dry tropical air and wet equatorial air

questions.question: What does 'cyclone' mean when talking about mid-latitude cyclones?
options: A high-pressure system with air spinning outwards
A low-pressure system with air spinning inwards
A storm that only happens in summer
A fast-moving warm front

subtopics.title: The Initial Stage - Drawing the Battle Lines

questions.question: In the Initial Stage of a mid-latitude cyclone, what are the two main winds blowing past each other?
options: Warm westerly winds and cold easterly winds
Warm easterly winds and cold westerly winds
Trade winds and monsoons
Northerly winds and southerly winds

questions.question: What do we call the line where the warm and cold air masses first meet without mixing?
options: The Equator
The Wave Front
The Polar Front
The Occluded Front

questions.question: At the Initial Stage, what is the movement of the air like along the Polar Front?
options: The cold air immediately pushes the warm air straight up
The warm and cold air blow past each other in opposite directions without mixing
The warm air sinks rapidly
The two air masses immediately mix together to form a storm

subtopics.title: The Wave Stage - A Kink in the Line

questions.question: What causes the initial 'kink' or wave to form on the Polar Front?
options: Friction between the two moving bodies of air
A sudden drop in temperature over the land
The warm air disappearing completely
Heavy rain starting over the ocean

questions.question: In which direction does a mid-latitude cyclone rotate in the Southern Hemisphere?
options: Clockwise
Anti-clockwise
Straight upwards
It does not rotate

questions.question: What begins to form at the center of the spinning wave?
options: A high-pressure center
A calm, cloudless area
A low-pressure center
An anticyclone

subtopics.title: The Mature Stage - The Engine is Roaring

questions.question: During the Mature Stage, how does the cold front behave compared to the warm front?
options: It bulldozes under the warm air, forcing it up quickly
It slides gently over the warm air
It moves backwards towards Antarctica
It mixes perfectly with the warm air

questions.question: What type of weather does the passing of the cold front typically bring?
options: Gentle, steady rain and flat stratus clouds
Clear skies and high temperatures
Heavy rain, thunderstorms, and a sharp drop in temperature
Dry, hot winds from the north

questions.question: How does the warm front behave in the Mature Stage?
options: It quickly bulldozes under the cold air
It slowly slides up over the back of the cold air
It stops moving completely
It brings freezing temperatures and snow

subtopics.title: The Occluded Stage - The End of the Trail

questions.question: What exactly happens during the Occluded Stage of a mid-latitude cyclone?
options: The warm front speeds up and leaves the cold front behind
The fast-moving cold front catches up to the slow-moving warm front
The storm hits the coast for the first time
The system starts rotating anti-clockwise

questions.question: What happens to the warm air during occlusion?
options: It sinks to the ground and gets hot
It is completely lifted off the ground
It pushes the cold air back to Antarctica
It stays exactly where it is

questions.question: Why does the storm lose its fuel and start to die off in the Occluded Stage?
options: Because all the warm air is pushed up and away, removing the energy source
Because the wind suddenly stops blowing completely
Because it hits high mountains
Because the sun comes out

subtopics.title: Why the Western Cape Gets Wet in Winter

questions.question: Why do mid-latitude cyclones only affect the Western Cape in winter?
options: Because the ocean only gets cold in winter
Because in summer, high-pressure belts shift south and block the cyclones
Because in winter, the cyclones move in from the Indian Ocean
Because the mountains grow taller in winter

questions.question: What happens to the pressure belts in winter to allow the cyclones to hit the Western Cape?
options: They shift south
They disappear completely
They shift north, opening the door for the cyclones
They merge into one giant low-pressure system

questions.question: When the cold front from a mid-latitude cyclone hits the Western Cape, what combination of weather occurs?
options: Temperatures drop, wind turns north-west, and heavy rain starts
Temperatures rise, wind drops, and clear skies appear
It gets very hot and dry with east winds
Gentle rain falls with no wind at all
